page.description: OpenBSD 7.8 installer: size, architecture, publisher SHA-256 and a licensed screenshot.
page.intro: A security-focused BSD with its own kernel and userland. The installer image is small; a desktop is added after the base system.
pros: Security-first defaults and a small, audited base system.
Documented, predictable release cadence with six-month support windows.
The installer is under a gigabyte.
One handbook covers the whole system.
cons: Not Linux: Linux drivers and tools do not apply.
No desktop on the installer; X and a window manager are added separately.
Hardware support is narrower than on Linux.
Each release is supported for about a year, so upgrades are routine.
page.previewNote: A stock screenshot of a Window Maker desktop on OpenBSD 6.5 from Wikimedia Commons. It is not 7.8 and not a ROMinit recording: no image was written and nothing was booted for this page.
